skill.name: using-superpowers
skill.description: Guides AI assistants to find, announce, and follow relevant skills before starting work.
skill.summary: Establishes a repeatable workflow for using AI skills and checklist tracking.
skill.author: DYAI2025

security_audit.summary: The static system-reconnaissance finding is a false positive because the referenced text only describes workflow discipline. The binary archive warning was manually reviewed, and SKILL.zip contains only the same SKILL.md content with no additional payload.

static_findings.snippet: **Many skills contain rigid rules (TDD, debugging, verification).** Follow them exactly. Don't adapt

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 54 discusses whether skills contain rigid or flexible workflow rules. It does not perform system reconnaissance, request environment details, or instruct data collection.
Manual archive review shows SKILL.zip contains only SKILL.md, and the archived file matches the reviewed SKILL.md content. No executable payload or hidden file was found.

low_findings.title: Unscanned file (binary) — manual review required
low_findings.confidence_reasoning: Force-confirmed metadata/low static finding; AI dismissal overridden.

content.value_statement: AI assistants can skip useful skill instructions when tasks move quickly. This skill creates a clear workflow for skill discovery, announcements, and checklist tracking.
actual_capabilities: Defines when an assistant should check for relevant skills before work starts.
Requires relevant skills to be read and followed before task execution.
Specifies clear announcements before a skill is used.
Requires separate TodoWrite items for every checklist step in a skill.
Explains how to treat rigid workflows and flexible skill patterns.
limitations: Does not execute tools or install skills by itself.
Does not provide project-specific coding or design instructions.
Requires an assistant environment that supports skills and task tracking.
May add process overhead for very small tasks.

use_cases.title: Onboard New AI Workflows
use_cases.description: Teach a team how an assistant should find, announce, and follow available skills before work begins.

use_cases.title: Track Checklist-Heavy Tasks
use_cases.description: Ensure every checklist item from a selected skill becomes visible work instead of hidden mental tracking.
use_cases.target_user: Developer using Claude Code or Codex

use_cases.title: Standardize Assistant Process
use_cases.description: Create consistent expectations for how assistants use skills across planning, coding, debugging, and verification tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Start With Skill Discovery
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when starting a simple task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the using-superpowers workflow for this task. First identify any relevant skills, then announce and follow them before starting work.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Enforce Checklist Tracking
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a selected skill includes checklist steps.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the using-superpowers workflow. If any chosen skill has a checklist, create separate task items for every checklist step.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Coordinate Multiple Skills
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a task may require several skill workflows.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the using-superpowers workflow to evaluate relevant skills, choose the minimum set needed, announce them, and follow each required workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Audit Process Compliance
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when reviewing whether an assistant followed skill rules.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this task against the using-superpowers workflow. Identify missed skill discovery, missing announcements, or unchecked checklist items.

output_examples.input: Start a refactor task with skill discipline.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies relevant skills, states which one applies, reads it, and creates visible checklist tasks before editing files.

output_examples.input: Use a testing skill that includes a checklist.
output_examples.output: The assistant creates one task item for each checklist step, then marks items complete only after finishing the work.

output_examples.input: Review whether the assistant followed process rules.
output_examples.output: The assistant reports whether skill discovery happened, whether skill usage was announced, and whether checklist steps were tracked.

best_practices: Read the current version of each relevant skill before applying it.
Announce selected skills clearly before using their workflow.
Track every checklist item as visible work, not as memory.
anti_patterns: Assuming a remembered skill is still current without reading it.
Skipping skill discovery because a task appears simple.
Combining several checklist items into one vague task item.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It tells an AI assistant how to find, announce, and follow relevant skills before starting a task.

faq.question: Does it write code or run commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow instructions for assistant behavior, not executable code or command automation.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: When is it most useful?
faq.answer: It is useful when tasks depend on skill-specific workflows, checklists, or repeatable assistant process rules.

faq.question: Does it replace project instructions?
faq.answer: No. It helps organize how the assistant uses skills while still following the user task and project context.

faq.question: Are there security concerns?
faq.answer: No evidence of malicious behavior was found. The archive contains only the reviewed SKILL.md content.
